name: RT-2 / Vision-Language-Action Models — Technical Summary + Current Tooling
observations: SOURCE: "RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control", Brohan et al. (Google DeepMind), 2023, arXiv:2307.15818v1, 26 pages. Local file: pdf/embodied_ai_papers/RT-2, Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control, Anthony Brohan et al., 2023, v1_compressed.pdf. Knowledge item created 2026-11-01.

CORE IDEA: A VLA (vision-language-action) model is a pretrained vision-language model co-fine-tuned to emit robot actions directly. Actions are expressed as text tokens and trained with the same next-token objective as language, so image + instruction -> low-level action runs end-to-end in one model with fully shared weights (no separate action head or action-only layers).

ACTION ENCODING (paper Sec. 3.2): 8 integers per step = [terminate, dpos_x, dpos_y, dpos_z, drot_x, drot_y, drot_z, gripper_extension]. 6-DoF end-effector delta pose + gripper + episode-termination flag; all continuous dims discretized into 256 uniform bins. Emitted as a whitespace-separated string, e.g. "1 128 91 241 5 101 127".

TOKEN MAPPING: 256 tokens must be reserved as action vocabulary. PaLI-X already has a unique token per integer up to 1000, so bins map to those integer tokens; PaLM-E has no such representation, so its 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten (a form of symbol tuning).

TRAINING FORMAT: robot camera image + instruction are posed in standard VQA form ("Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A: <action tokens>"), so manipulation data becomes another vision-language task.
BACKBONES: RT-2-PaLI-X built on PaLI-X (5B and 55B); RT-2-PaLM-E built on PaLM-E 12B. Both are {image, text} -> {text} VLMs.

CO-FINE-TUNING IS THE KEY TRICK: fine-tune on robot trajectories *mixed with* the original web-scale VLM data (VQA, captioning, interleaved image-text) instead of robot data alone. This prevents catastrophic forgetting of web concepts and measurably improves generalization; the robot dataset is up-weighted in each batch to keep the mixture balanced.

OUTPUT CONSTRAINT: at decode time the vocabulary is restricted to valid action tokens when the prompt is a robot-action task, while language/VQA prompts still allow the full natural-language vocabulary. Guarantees executable actions.

REAL-TIME INFERENCE: the 55B model is served on a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network (simultaneously serving multiple robots), giving 1-3 Hz for 55B and ~5 Hz for 5B. Compute cost/latency is the main deployment constraint.

DATA & EVAL SCALE: ~6,000 real-robot evaluation trajectories; training data is the RT-1 dataset (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen) plus web VLM data; 7-DoF mobile manipulator; 200+ seen tasks and 280+ unseen tasks.

RESULTS: seen-task performance roughly matches RT-1, but generalization to unseen objects/backgrounds/environments is ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO and ~6x better than other baselines. Emergent symbol understanding ("move apple to 3"), reasoning (same-color matching, arithmetic, multilingual commands) and human recognition average >3x RT-1's success rate.

ABLATIONS: 55B > 5B for generalization; training a large model from scratch performs poorly even at 5B; co-fine-tuning beats robot-only fine-tuning at every size. Simulated Language-Table: RT-2-PaLI-3B 90+-10 vs LAVA 77, RT-1 74, BC-Zero 72.

CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT: a few hundred gradient steps of data augmented with a natural-language "Plan:" step before the action tokens ("Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: ...") bridges VQA-style reasoning and manipulation, enabling multi-stage semantic inference (pick a rock as an improvised hammer; choose an energy drink for a tired person).

LIMITATIONS: web pretraining transfers semantic/visual concepts but no new *physical* skills — the motion repertoire stays bounded by the robot dataset; inference compute/latency limits high-frequency control (quantization/distillation flagged as future work); few VLMs expose fine-tuning APIs.

MODERN EQUIVALENTS (verified in Context7 docs, 2026-11): Hugging Face LeRobot (/huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1) is the closest current best-practice stack — `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=...` or `--policy.type=pi0 --policy.pretrained_path=lerobot/pi0_base`, plus dataset/env flags and standard steps/batch_size hyperparameters.

MODERN SERVING PATTERN: LeRobot async inference (install `.[async]`) splits a GPU policy server (`python -m lerobot.async_inference.policy_server --host --port`) from a robot client (`python -m lerobot.async_inference.robot_client --server_address --policy_type=smolvla|pi0 --actions_per_chunk=50 --chunk_size_threshold=0.5 --aggregate_fn_name=weighted_average`) — the direct descendant of RT-2's cloud-served 55B model. `--inference.type=rtc` (real-time chunking) is recommended for large slow VLAs (Pi0, Pi0.5, SmolVLA) to keep motion smooth despite latency.

MODERN BACKBONE PATH: Transformers (/websites/huggingface_co_transformers_v4_56_2_en) PaliGemma / PaliGemma2 via `image-text-to-text` pipeline or `PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration` + `PaliGemmaProcessor`; note PaliGemma is not conversational and is meant to be fine-tuned per task (VQA, captioning, detection), and the processor's `suffix=` argument generates fine-tuning labels — the natural place to put action-token targets.

PRACTICAL MAPPING OF RT-2 RECIPE TODAY: (1) collect demonstrations in LeRobot dataset format with language instructions; (2) start from a VLM-backed policy (SmolVLA, pi0/pi0.5) and keep VLM weights loaded; (3) co-train on task data plus general VLM/VQA data to preserve semantics; (4) constrain decoding to the action vocabulary and discretize/bucket continuous action dims; (5) serve the policy on a GPU host via the async server and stream action chunks to the robot.
VERIFICATION CAVEAT: OpenVLA could not be confirmed — the Context7 resolver returned unrelated libraries (OpenClaw/OpenLayers/OpenBLAS) for that name, so no OpenVLA documentation was verified here.

name: LeRobot
observations: Hugging Face LeRobot — end-to-end learning for robotics; Context7 ID /huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1, High source reputation, ~4543 code snippets.

Provides `lerobot-train` CLI with policy types including smolvla, pi0, pi05, act; supports loading pretrained VLM weights, gradient checkpointing, bfloat16, frozen/unfrozen vision encoders, and train-expert-only modes.

Provides async inference (policy_server + robot_client over gRPC) and real-time chunking (RTC) for high-latency VLA policies; key tuning knobs are actions_per_chunk, chunk_size_threshold, aggregate_fn_name.
Documented datasets include lerobot/libero, lerobot/libero_plus, lerobot/metaworld_mt50 with matching env types for sim evaluation.

name: Hugging Face Transformers (PaliGemma / VLM models)
observations: Context7 ID /websites/huggingface_co_transformers_v4_56_2_en — model-definition framework for text, vision, audio and multimodal models, ~11081 code snippets, High reputation.
PaliGemma/PaliGemma2 are supported as image-text-to-text models via `pipeline(task="image-text-to-text")` or `PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration` + `AutoProcessor`.
PaliGemma is not designed as a conversational model; it performs best when fine-tuned for a specific task such as VQA, captioning, detection, or document understanding.
PaliGemmaProcessor handles images, text, and optional labels; passing `suffix=` produces the labels used during fine-tuning — the mechanism to adapt to text-encoded action targets.
